    Reference · questions · vocabulary

    FAQ & glossary

    Straight answers to the questions new owners ask — mock mode, keys and cost, sleeping laptops, PDFs, backups, what the board does with your uploads, what Mix does, what the Fund is and whether its tax numbers are real, what the SPOTLIGHT chip on a lead means and whether its prices are tradeable — and a glossary of every term the board uses, from grade and stance to basis, ratchet, horizon class, beta, read-across, the mandate, allocation and tax lots.

    Questions#

    Why does it start in mock mode, and what is mock mode?#

    Because there is no API key yet. Without ANTHROPIC_API_KEY the app swaps every language-model call for deterministic heuristics written in each persona’s spirit — Flow keys off volume-over-open-interest, Dagger off RSI and momentum, Sam punishes counter-trend setups, the Skeptic inverts the room, the Executive takes a weighted blend. The pipeline, the sessions, the Pulse rationales and the court all run; market data is live; output has the same shape; the UI shows a MOCK MODE pill. It costs nothing and is how most of this Guide was exercised. Add a key (how) and restart for the real board; set BABLYTICS_MOCK=1 to stay in mock mode with a key present.

    Does Bablytics trade for me?#

    No. It is a research tool. The morning pipeline, the Pulse, the Bailiff and the Paper League have no execution path at all — nothing in those modules can reach a venue. The one place the app touches a real account is the Broker view, and only if you connect your own Schwab developer app: the bot stages orders from the morning leads, and you may submit one order per click behind a confirmation that restates ticker, side, quantity and price. There is no submit-all, no server-side loop over orders and no auto-submit setting. A submitted order is your decision on your account. See Not financial advice.

    What does an API key mean, and what does it cost?#

    A key is a credential from your own Anthropic account; calls are billed to you by token at Anthropic’s current rates for the model in use (default claude-opus-4-8; change it with BABLYTICS_MODEL). Bablytics does not quote prices because they are Anthropic’s to set — check their pricing page. What you can budget is volume: in real mode a weekday makes on the order of 60–75 calls (fifteen each for the morning briefing, Pre-Open Check, Midday Check-In and Evening Court, one more each morning for the book’s read-across, one per Pulse cycle), each with a long prompt — longer when you have evidence on file — plus weekend horizon panels and anything you trigger by hand. Mock mode makes zero.

    Can it keep its schedule while my laptop is asleep or closed?#

    No. The schedule is a set of cron jobs inside the app; they fire while the app is open and the machine is awake. A job missed during sleep is skipped, not replayed. Every session has a Run now button for exactly that, and the record is honest about gaps — the Archive marks sessions that never ran rather than hiding them. If you want the full rhythm unattended, run it on a machine that stays on.

    Where do the PDFs go?#

    Wherever your browser saves downloads. Each export asks for a password of at least 4 characters and encrypts the file with it; the app streams it to you and keeps no copy. In the desktop window (2.0 and later) the embedded web view is allowed to download, so a Save dialog opens, defaulting to your Downloads folder. If no dialog appears — an older build, or a web view that refuses downloads — open http://127.0.0.1:8420 (or the port in the log) in your regular browser, sign in, and export there — same server, same file.

    How do I get the reports without running the app?#

    Join the mailing list on Get the reports by email: Sean sends the Morning Briefing PDF each trading day, the Evening Court and the weekend Week in Review / Week Ahead from his own copy of the app — by hand, after each session, never by a schedule. Name and email only, never sold; the list is a create-only Firestore collection that only he can read, and the app's Mailing list tab is where he syncs it and clicks Send on each batch. They are research reports from an AI boardroom, not advice — the same PDFs the app exports, with the same disclaimer on every page. Reply STOP to any report or use the unsubscribe page to leave.

    How do I back it up or move it to another computer?#

    Quit, copy the data folder (paths per OS). That is everything: account, record, journals, models, keys. Restore by copying it back, or point BABLYTICS_DATA_DIR at it. Details in Data & privacy.

    I forgot my password.#

    There is no reset — nobody but you holds anything. The only route is a fresh data folder, which loses the record. Write the password down when you create the account.

    Does it work offline?#

    The UI, the Archive, the Library, the journals and the Guide do. Anything that needs the tape does not: the scan, the levels, the Pulse, the League marks. A morning run with no network falls back to a synthetic candidate list so the pipeline can still be demonstrated, and says so.

    How does the Pulse know what I hold?#

    Only from what you tell it inside the app: holdings you upload on Positions (CSV or a Schwab export), trades you log by hand with Log a trade, and leads you mark TAKEN. It never reads the broker connection. With an empty book it runs watch-only over the day’s leads.

    Does the board actually read what I upload?#

    The text of it, yes — in AI mode. A PDF or a text, markdown, CSV or JSON file you drop into the Evidence locker has its text extracted (PDFs: the first 60 pages, 20 000 characters per file) and appended, with your note, to every grader prompt and the Executive’s prompt as a USER EVIDENCE section, and to the Evening Court’s prompts if the document is flagged Evening; the block as a whole is capped at 12 000 characters and the seats are told to cite a document by name when it changes a grade. Images and audio are stored and listed but not read yet — the board reads your note on them, and the panel says so. In mock mode nothing is read and no grade moves; the mock memo just names the documents on file. Preview what the committee sees under the list shows the exact block. Files never leave your data folder; only the extracted text travels, only inside a prompt, only with a key — see Data & privacy.

    What does “SWING · ≈5 sessions” mean, and why is it not the option’s expiry?#

    It is the lead’s time horizon: the board’s class for the trade (intraday, swing, position, long-term) and the number of sessions it expects the target to take, with a band and a one-line basis in the expanded lead. It is a statement about the thesis, not the contract. On an option lead the horizon must fit inside the contract — never longer than DTE − 1 sessions, clamped if the board overreached — but a nine-day contract can carry a three-session thesis. When the board did not state a horizon (mock mode, older runs) the app estimates one from the ATR distance to the target, or from the DTE, and labels the basis estimated. The Evening Court does not yet score it against what happened; that is on the backlog.

    What does Mix do?#

    Mix is the default mandate — the fourth position of the MANDATE knob in the dashboard header (Day · Swing · Long-term · Mix), also on Settings. A fixed mandate tells the board to write the whole book on one clock: Day trade admits only intraday leads and 0–5-day contracts, Swing only swing leads (intraday tolerated) and 6–30-day contracts, Long-term only position and long-term leads with 45–180-day contracts; under those, every seat grades each candidate for fit, the Executive’s Top 20 must fit, and the slate drops off-mandate leads before it fills the ten-plus-ten. Mix does the opposite of narrowing: every horizon class is allowed, nothing is graded down for its clock, and instead the board is asked to spread the book — at least 3 intraday, 8 swing and 4 position / long-term leads when the candidates allow — and to state the split in the memo. Each lead’s option contract is then picked in the window of its own class (0–5, 6–30 or 45–180 days). The run records the split it achieved (book_split), and under Mix no card ever wears the off-mandate chip. If you want one kind of book, pick that kind; Mix is for owners who want the board to find the best trade on each clock and let them choose. Mechanism: Morning Briefing.

    Why is a lead’s horizon chip greyed out and titled “off-mandate”?#

    Because the run was generated under a fixed mandate and that lead’s horizon class falls outside it — it was admitted only because fewer than twenty candidates fit the mandate, and its executive summary ends with the same tag. In mock mode such a lead also carries a grade no higher than 55 (the off-mandate cap); in AI mode the seats were told to grade it down for fit and say “off-mandate” in their comments. The chip tells you the board knew. Change the knob and the next run is generated for the new mandate; the run you are looking at keeps saying what it was generated under. Never shown under Mix.

    Why does the Bailiff say “dry run”?#

    Because enforcement is opt-in. bailiff_dry_run defaults to on, so the scheduled passes evaluate every written invalidation against the tape and report armed/fired/pending/unenforceable without changing a row. Even live, the Bailiff closes legs in the record only — the board’s own book and the Paper League — never a real position. See The Bailiff.

    What is the Fund, and how is it different from the Paper League?#

    The Fund is one synthetic paper book. It admits every lead the board finally grades 60 or better — one slot per underlying, capped at twenty — fills it on paper at the next session’s open, and then holds it on that lead’s own stop, target and stated horizon instead of a flat calendar rule. Once a day, at 17:10 ET, it marks the book, applies the exits that fired on a close, admits what the board added, and asks a small transformer what fraction of the portfolio belongs in the book at all. The Paper League is fifteen books scoring fifteen philosophies with deliberately crude rules — three picks each, 10 % per leg, a five-day hold. The Fund scores the room’s signed ≥60 book as one managed portfolio, with sizing decided by a model and exits decided by what the board actually wrote. Side-by-side comparison: The League and the Fund. Both are paper by construction; neither has an execution path. And with only a few dozen genuine sessions behind it, the Fund’s allocation is deliberately shrunk halfway toward a prior built from your own risk and size goals — the dial says shrunk when it is doing that, which today is always.

    The Fund says it “held for tax”. Are those tax numbers real?#

    They are estimates, not tax advice, and the Fund itself is synthetic paper money with no tax liability of any kind. What the tax lens does is make one real effect visible: before executing a trim or an exit the model proposed, the reweight prices the realized gain or loss, estimates the tax at that lot’s term — short-term under 365 days, long-term at or beyond, at the flat rates in Settings (defaults 37 % / 20 %, plus a state rate you can set) — and compares the after-tax edge against a hysteresis threshold (default 0.15 % of fund equity). Below the threshold the lot is held and the order log says so in words: “held for tax: realizing $412 would cost $152 in estimated tax; the model’s edge was only $96.” It knows nothing about your bracket, your account type, your carry-forwards or anything you hold outside the app, and its wash-sale flag is a disclosure, not a rule it enforces. Rates and thresholds are settings in your own database and, like everything else, never leave your machine.

    A lead card has a SPOTLIGHT chip. What is that?#

    It means that lead was graded 60 or better, so the app wrote a full strategy profile for it — a Spotlight. Click the chip and you get the setup and the dated catalyst, what the options market is pricing against what the name has actually done on its last ten earnings prints, a table of structures priced off the chain that was really pulled (each one scored twice: under the market’s implied distribution and against that history), and the nine conditions — intraday · swing · long-term against conservative · moderate · aggressive — with your own cell ringed and the other eight still readable. Sixty is deliberately the same line the Fund admits on: the setting is spotlight_min_grade and it defaults to the same 60 as fund_min_grade. The chip also shows in the Archive, in the Fund’s holdings and in the briefing PDF, and it opens a document — nothing more.

    Can I trade a spotlight’s structures at the prices it prints?#

    No — and the document says so on its own last page. Every premium in a spotlight is the contract’s last traded price from the chain pull, not a live quote: it may be hours or days old, the real bid/ask is wider, and on a weekend pull the whole table is stale by construction. Open interest frequently comes back as zero for an entire chain, which means the crowding check the desk normally runs cannot be run at all. The historical column is ten prints — a story, not a distribution — and the probability and expected-value columns assume the market’s own implied distribution is the true one, which, if it were reliably true, would leave no structure with an edge at all, that one included. Cells that should not be traded say no position and give the reason rather than inventing something. Treat the whole document as research: it is model output, not advice, and no part of Bablytics places, stages or routes an order. See the honest limits.

    The Watchdog says “no signal”. Is something broken?#

    It has no data source. Live congressional disclosures need a Quiver Quantitative key (QUIVER_API_KEY); the free legacy dumps the collector falls back to currently answer 403. Everything else runs without it.

    Why does a view say “the court has not yet convened”?#

    That session has not run yet today — it is scheduled for later, the app was closed at the time, or there was no morning run to score. Press the session’s Run now button, or wait.

    Is the S&P 500 list kept current?#

    The scan universe is a constituent snapshot baked into the code (503 tickers as of 2026-08-18). From a source checkout, python -m bablytics.universe refresh re-fetches it from Wikipedia into data/universe.json, which then overrides the snapshot; the desktop app has no button for it.

    Can two people share one install?#

    It is built single-user: one account per data folder, one board, one record. Two people means two data folders (two BABLYTICS_DATA_DIRs, or two machines).

    Glossary#

    Grouped by where you meet the word. Terms link to the page that explains the mechanism.

    Grading and the board#

    grade
    A member’s 0–100 score for one candidate. 50 is neutral; the further from 50, the stronger the view. The Executive’s final grade is the number on the card and the ranking key.
    stance
    bull, bear or neutral — the direction of a member’s grade, separate from its size. Bull with 80 and bear with 20 are both strong.
    conviction
    |grade − 50| / 50: how far a member leaned, 0 to 1. It sizes paper-league picks and the Pyramid’s scoring.
    grade range
    The lowest and highest grade any seat gave a lead (“board range 58–76”), drawn as a rail under the final grade so you see the disagreement, not just the average.
    consensus strip
    The expanded lead’s wide rail with every member’s emoji placed at their own grade; colliding emoji stack rather than overlap, and each is a link to that member’s comment.
    calibration
    Per-member stats over their graded leads: sample size, hit rate, average grade, and the correlation between their grades and realized returns. The Executive reads it and discounts consistently wrong seats.
    the Skeptic
    The seat that grades after all thirteen graders, with their grades in hand, and is paid to attack. Ranked on the Pyramid; has a paper book; does not chair.
    the Executive
    The chair. Weighs the graders by calibration and pyramid rank, reads the Skeptic and the outcome model, signs the final ranked 20 and writes the memo with the day’s house rules. Not ranked on the Pyramid — the ranking is theirs to answer for.
    the Pyramid
    The daily ranking of every grader and the Skeptic by stance sign × conviction × underlying move, smoothed as an EWMA over ten sessions and cut into tiers. Rank 1 is “in charge of the world today” and the Executive is told to weight that seat more. See The board.
    journal · lesson
    Each member’s Evening Court entry — on base, off base, and the durable lesson — persisted per member; the five most recent lessons are injected into that member’s next grading prompt.
    dossier
    A member’s full record: stat tiles, track record of graded leads with realized returns, journal timeline — in the app at #/member/<key> and as a markdown file under members/.
    house rules
    The memo’s closing block: stakes discipline, exit rules and windfall policy decided before the open, never mid-session. The Croupier’s doctrine made procedural.
    Standing Read
    A paragraph in the owner’s live-board briefing document (built outside the app, in data/boardroom/<date>/): where the index majors actually sit — levels, day/5-day/21-day moves, position in their 20-day range, VIX — before anyone describes a mood, with a written falsifier. Not an app feature: nothing in the pipeline, the dashboard or the later sessions produces or reads one.
    candidate · lead · slate
    A candidate is one of the ~40 names the scan surfaces; a lead is one of the 20 the board keeps — ten option leads with a selected contract (the options desk) and ten stock leads (the stock book). Each ticker takes at most one slot.
    the mandate
    The owner’s stated trading style for a run — Day trade, Swing, Long-term or Mix — as the board receives it: a MANDATE section in every grader’s, the Skeptic’s and the Executive’s prompt naming the style and its expected hold (same session · 2–10 sessions · weeks to months · any), the rule that a thesis needing a longer or shorter hold is graded down for fit (“off-mandate” in the comment), the requirement that every ranked lead’s horizon class be one the mandate allows (intraday; swing with intraday tolerated; position and long-term; Mix: all, spread ≥ 3 / ≥ 8 / ≥ 4), the option DTE window for contract selection (0–5 · 6–30 · 45–180 · per lead under Mix), and the memo’s first line. Every run stores the mandate it was generated under with its book_split. In mock mode the fit rule is arithmetic: +3 matched, 0 tolerated, −10 and capped at 55 off-mandate. An instruction about the kind of research book to write, not an order. Page.
    one bet in two slots
    The board’s phrase for the same read expressed twice — a stock and its option, or two names riding one macro driver (NEM and a GLD call are one gold bet). Covering the wheel, not diversifying; the Executive is told to rank them as one bet with the best expression on top.
    variance instrument
    From the owner’s paper Hedging the Wheel: diversification narrows the spread of outcomes around the same expectation; it cannot change a mean. A book of many copies of one bet is not safer, only more expensive.
    Dubins–Savage bold play
    The Croupier’s theorem: without a positive edge, the chance of reaching a target is maximised by the fewest, largest bets followed by exit; spreading thin is provably worse. Hence “concentrated, defined-risk, pre-committed exit” beats “a little of everything”.
    ratchet
    A pre-committed profit rule — “bank half above 2×, trail the rest at 40% off the high” — that harvests variance only on concentrated high-variance positions. The Bailiff’s 14:35 crude check reports BANK-HALF against the written rail and executes nothing.

    Levels, risk and the record#

    entry · now
    Entry is the pre-open price a lead was written at; now is the live print with the direction-signed % from entry. On option leads both describe the underlying.
    ATR(14)
    The 14-day Average True Range — the stock’s typical daily travel. Every stop and target is a multiple of it, printed so you can size the zone yourself.
    exit zone · ATR zone
    Stop and target as ATR multiples anchored on entry and signed by direction: conservative 1.0 / 1.5, moderate 1.5 / 2.5, aggressive 2.0 / 4.0. Arithmetic from one shared function, so the briefing, the dashboard cards and the Pulse cannot disagree. It is a mechanical bracket, not the written invalidation.
    horizon class · expected hold
    How long a lead is supposed to take to reach its target: a class — intraday, swing, position, long_term — an expected number of sessions (0.5 = same day), a human window (“2–5 sessions”, “3–8 weeks”) and a one-sentence basis (DTE, ATR-per-day distance, a catalyst date). Stated by the Executive in AI mode and estimated from the numbers otherwise; an option lead’s horizon never exceeds DTE − 1. Shown as the card chip and the overlay’s Expected-hold row. Page.
    contract mark
    An option lead’s live premium from the chain, shown beside the underlying’s levels.
    implied move
    What the options market is charging for an event: the at-the-money straddle (the call plus the put at the strike nearest spot, for the expiry that covers the catalyst) divided by the spot price, read as a ± percentage. NVDA’s 8/28 straddle at 13.25 against a 214.72 spot is an implied move of ±6.17%. It is the crowd’s own sigma, not a forecast, and a Spotlight uses it twice: as the width of the distribution every structure is scored under, and as the number to hold against what the name has actually done on its last ten prints (NVDA: 6.52% mean absolute over ten, 4.99% over the last six). When those two agree, nobody is being handed free money.
    barbell
    A structure that sells the middle of a distribution and buys back its tail: an iron condor body (short a put and a call, long the wings) where part of the credit pays for a cheap far out-of-the-money option in the direction the name’s fat tail has historically run. It exists because premium sellers are not killed by ordinary moves but by the one print in ten that goes +16%. In the reference study the 9/04 condor plus a single 8/28 235 call at 1.10 turned that quarter from the worst case (−581 per contract) into the best one (+802), and it was the only structure on an eleven-row menu positive under both the implied distribution and the name’s own history while keeping reward-to-risk above 1. It dies in the medium move — six to ten percent, which is exactly where the implied move sat. Page.
    kill · invalidation
    The thesis-killing condition the board writes for every lead in prose (“RTX closes below 219.00”), plus a structured trigger object. It is the board’s commitment, distinct from the mechanical exit zone. When it prints, the leg closes in the record.
    basis
    What a trigger is measured against: close (the 16:00 print — can never fire on an intraday tick), intraday (any print), or settle (the 14:30 ET futures settlement, for crude and gold rails). When the prose is ambiguous the parser chooses close, the conservative one.
    armed · fired · pending · unenforceable
    The Bailiff’s verdicts. Armed: watchable and not yet hit. Fired: the basis price crossed the level. Pending: the basis is not observable yet (a close rule before 16:00). Unenforceable: a real ruling no machine can watch — “one concrete de-escalation headline” — kept and shown, never dropped.
    OI conversion
    The Pre-Open audit of yesterday’s option-volume spike: did the volume become held open interest overnight (a confirmed position) or vanish (a pump fake)? A held ratio under 0.35 means it did not convert.
    gap zone
    Where a pre-market or opening print sits against the prior day’s range: above the high, in the upper range, in the lower range, or below the low. The Glazier’s read, and one of the Pulse’s input features.
    outcome (1d · 5d)
    A lead’s realized return one and five trading days after its run date, sign-flipped for shorts, recorded at 16:45 and used to train the outcome model, grade the board, and settle the League.
    Spearman
    Rank correlation. The live-board court documents report it between the board’s final grades and the day’s signed returns (the own-grades-versus-outcomes check); the app’s own calibration tiles use the ordinary (Pearson) kind. The round-22 fitness fix was verified once by Spearman and recorded in MODEL-CARD.md; nothing in the running code computes it.
    regime
    The one-line read of the index tape — “risk-on: SPY +2.1% 5d, VIX 14.2 falling” — on every briefing and every Pulse payload.
    beta · correlation (90-session)
    Beta is the slope of a lead’s daily returns on another symbol’s — SPY, QQQ, IWM, its sector ETF — by ordinary least squares over the last 90 sessions of aligned dates; 1.3 to SPY means the name has tended to move 1.3% for the index’s 1%. Correlation is how tightly, −1 to 1. Fewer than 60 overlapping sessions → null, not a guess. The card tag β 1.3 · XLK is beta to SPY and the sector ETF. Statistical coupling, not causation.
    read-across · coupling
    What else moves when this lead moves: the betas and correlations above, up to six sector peers ranked by correlation, an implied-move table (“if the lead moves +1% → SPY +0.4, XLK +0.6, MSFT +0.8”), a watch-also list (top three peers plus the sector ETF), and a two-to-three-sentence paragraph in the Executive’s voice on what a confirmed move would say about the market and the economy, with a macro line. Computed after grading and stored on the lead. Page.

    Sessions#

    Morning Briefing
    ~7:00 ET weekdays: collectors → candidates → graders → Skeptic → Executive → 20 leads + memo. Page.
    Pre-Open Check
    9:15 ET: the full committee revalidates the briefing against futures, pre-market prints, the OI-conversion audit, analyst moves, econ prints and fresh headlines; verdict confirmed move / pump fake / undecided, per-lead actions. Page.
    Midday Check-In
    12:30 ET: every seat reads its own open paper positions at the midday mark, files a hold-or-close per position (closes land on the paper ledger) and a risk tilt; the Executive synthesises. Page.
    Outcomes
    16:45 ET: realized 1d/5d returns are recorded, the League is marked, the outcome model retrains when there is enough data.
    Evening Court
    ~19:00 ET: the day is scored against the close, the Pyramid re-forms, every member journals, dossiers refresh, and the Pulse population runs one generation of training. Page.
    horizon review
    The weekend and period editions: Saturday week-in-review (backward), Sunday week-ahead prospectus (forward), plus month and year editions on the period boundaries. Page.
    RTH · ET
    Regular trading hours, 9:30–16:00 Eastern Time. Every clock in the app is America/New_York.

    Engines#

    the Pulse
    Half-hourly research feedback on your book during RTH: the committee’s standing views blended with a five-model actor-critic population, shaped by your goals, emitting bounded leans with ATR exit zones. No execution path. Page.
    lean
    The Pulse’s bounded vocabulary: enter, add, hold, trim, exit. A model view, not an instruction. Caution overrides cap enter/add at hold when VIX, SPY, the board grade or ensemble agreement say so.
    goals (risk × size)
    Your two stated preferences — conservative / moderate / aggressive, small / medium / large — stored as settings; they pick the ATR bracket and the training reward’s drawdown penalty. Not a suitability assessment.
    agreement
    The fraction of the five population members voting with the consensus. At or below 0.6 (a 3/2 split) the ensemble is not allowed to be aggressive.
    generation · fitness · held-out gate
    One nightly cycle of the population: score every member (fitness, dominated by held-out shaped reward), train, breed a child from the best, and admit it only if it beats the worst on the frozen held-out split. Elitism is absolute; every decision, including no-ops, is recorded. Page.
    the Bailiff
    The officer of the court: parses written invalidations into triggers, watches the tape every 15 minutes during RTH, sweeps close-basis rules at 16:05, and enforces in the record only. Page.
    dry run
    The Bailiff’s default: evaluate and report, change nothing. Live enforcement is an explicit opt-in per machine.
    Paper League
    Fifteen autonomous $100,000 paper books — the thirteen graders, the Skeptic and the Bot — opened from each morning’s leads, held five trading days, marked at 16:45. A self-scoring simulation, not money. Page.
    paper fill
    The League’s entry rule: that day’s official open, sized at 10% of the member’s equity. A run made before the open leaves the position pending until the open bar exists — no invented prices.
    the Bot
    The League account that mechanically trades the Executive’s signed book — top five by final grade, 60 or better — so the chair’s ranking is scored as a book, not just a list.
    the Fund · admission
    The Fund is one synthetic paper book holding the board’s ≥60 leads on their own written terms. Admission is its entry rule: a lead whose final grade is at or above fund_min_grade (default 60) on a completed morning run, for an underlying the Fund does not already hold — one slot per name, so an option lead and its stock are one bet and the better expression takes the slot — up to fund_max_positions (default 20). An admitted lot fills at the next session’s open and carries the lead’s stop, target, horizon and written invalidation unchanged. Exits are checked on a close: stop, target, horizon expiry (with 25 % slack), the Bailiff’s kill, grade decay below 50, option expiry. Model opinion, not advice; nothing executes. Page.
    allocation (a) · weights
    The Fund’s two model outputs. Allocation a ∈ [0, 1] is the share of a notional portfolio the transformer says belongs in the fund today — the Fund’s answer to how much, where the Pulse answers what to do. Weights wi, summing to 1, split the fund’s own capital across its open lots, so the exposure of a lot is a × wi. While the training sample is below fund_min_train_days the deployed allocation is shrunk halfway toward a prior from your risk and size goals, and the payload says "shrunk": true and why. Page.
    tax lot · term
    One paper position opened at one fill price on one date, tracked with opened_on, quantity and basis, and on exit closed_on, proceeds, realized P&L and term — short when the lot was held under 365 days, long at or beyond it, taxed in the Fund’s estimates at fund_tax_short_rate / fund_tax_long_rate plus a state rate. A proposed trim that would realize a gain is checked for after-tax edge against a hysteresis threshold before it executes; below it the lot is held for tax and the order log says by how much. Estimates for a synthetic book — never tax advice. Page.
    wash-sale risk
    A disclosure, not a rule the app enforces. When the Fund closes a lot at a loss it marks that underlying; if the board grades the same name ≥60 again within fund_wash_days (default 30) the Fund still admits it — it is synthetic, and refusing would distort the board’s record — but flags the order and the holding wash_risk with the sentence spelled out: a repurchase inside 30 days would disallow that loss in a taxable account. Real wash-sale rules are more intricate than one date window; this is a flag to make you look, not a determination. Page.
    mock mode
    The no-key mode: deterministic heuristic personas in place of language-model calls, identical output shape, zero API cost, MOCK MODE pill in the UI.

    The desk and the app#

    TAKE · taken
    The toggle on a lead card that marks it as a trade you actually made. Taken leads join the Pulse’s book and, once their 1-day outcome lands, owe a reflection.
    reflection
    Your own journal: what happened, and — required when you lost — what you would do differently. Handed verbatim to the Executive’s Evening Court prompt. A taken trade with a reflection cannot be un-taken.
    staged order
    An order the bot drafts from a morning lead into the Broker queue. It goes nowhere until you click Submit on that one order and confirm; it can be edited or cancelled first. Page.
    spotlight
    The full strategy profile written for every lead the board grades at or above spotlight_min_grade — default 60, deliberately the same line as the Fund’s fund_min_grade admission, so “above sixty” means one thing in this app. Generated after a completed run persists, and on demand; one row per lead per run, upserted on a re-run. It carries the setup, the dated catalyst, the implied move against the name’s last ten earnings reactions, a structure table priced off the real chain, the nine conditions, one recommendation per horizon with where it dies, the read-across, the board’s split and the caveats — in the app at #/spotlight/<lead_id> and as Bablytics-Spotlight-<TICKER>-<date>.pdf. A SPOTLIGHT chip marks the lead wherever it appears. Research output with no order path. Page.
    the nine conditions
    A spotlight’s 3 × 3 grid: rows are the owner’s horizon — intraday 0–5 DTE, swing 6–30, long_term 45–180, straight from config.CLASS_DTE — and columns the owner’s risk — conservative 1.0/1.5, moderate 1.5/2.5, aggressive 2.0/4.0 ATR for stop/target, straight from pulse.goals.EXIT_ZONE_ATR. Neither axis is invented for the page; both are the house tables the contract scanner and the exit zone already use, so the grid is derived. Each cell carries an instrument (shares, or a contract that exists in the pull), a structure, entry, stop and target as prices, the move required in percent, a size hint, one sentence of what it needs to win, and a viability flag — and a cell that should not be traded reads “no position” with the reason instead of inventing one. Your own risk and size settings ring one cell as “your stated profile”; the other eight stay on the page, because the owner asked for all nine. Page.
    the Archive
    The historical record, browsable by day: every briefing, pre-open, midday, court, journal and Bailiff docket, with sessions that never ran marked rather than hidden. Page.
    the Library
    Where each seat’s thinking comes from — origin, why it matters, reading list — and the Borges story the product is named for.
    Curry cycle
    A hand-posted market-cycle forecast (author, text, target date) from Settings; the Timekeeper reads the five most recent beside its own frequency decomposition.
    trading style · MANDATE knob
    The setting behind the mandate: trading_style in the settings table — intraday (Day trade), swing, long_term, mix (the default) — set with the four-way segmented control right of the Morning | Evening toggle in the dashboard header, or on Settings; saved at once (/api/settings/mandate) with the toast “Next briefing will be generated for …”, read by the pipeline at run time, never re-grading a run that already exists. The briefing header prints “Generated under …” from the run and a muted “next run: …” when the knob has moved since. Page.
    universe
    The set of tickers the morning scan covers: an S&P 500 snapshot baked into the code (503 names), overridable by data/universe.json.
    data folder
    The one directory holding the database, caches, models, dossiers, logs and your .env. Page.
    Evidence locker · USER EVIDENCE
    The dashboard panel where you drop files for the committee — PDF, text/markdown/CSV/JSON, images, audio (25 MB each) — with a note, Morning and Evening flags and an optional expiry. Extracted text and notes ride every board prompt and the court prompts as a USER EVIDENCE section (12 000 characters, oldest trimmed first) that the seats must weigh and cite by name; images and audio contribute the note only in v1. Files stay under uploads/ in the data folder. Page.
    Listen
    The memo’s read-aloud control: the browser’s speech engine, with a voice picker and rate, so the briefing can be heard while you do something else.
